name: Minimalism
summary: Flat, exact, repeated forms: stripes, grids and bare shapes in one or two colours. The picture is an object with no story and no hand, and the viewer sees what is there.

philosophy.core_thesis: A picture is a plain object: what you see is what is there, so that form is reduced to the fewest parts and no illusion, gesture or story remains.
design_principles: Reduce the picture to 1–3 elements: a stripe, a grid, a bar or a single shape.
Repeat one unit, such as a stripe of 40–80mm, 8–40 times, in a strict order.
Paint flat, even coats with no stroke, and keep the edge sharp to under 1mm.
Limit the colour to 1–3 hues, or to black, grey and white, with no mixing and no gradient.
Let the shape of the canvas follow the pattern: a notched, shaped or very wide support is fine.
Fix the system before the painting starts, and follow it with no change by taste.
Give the picture no title that tells a story and no sign of the hand.
anti_patterns: A gesture, a drip or a visible stroke
A figure, an object or a landscape
A soft, blended or glowing edge
A rich, many-hued or decorative palette
A title that tells a story or a feeling

composition.layout: A repeated stripe or grid on a flat support, in a fixed order, with an even spacing and no focal centre.
composition.focal_point: None: the field is even; the eye goes to the edge of the support and to the single change in the pattern.
composition.format: A square or very wide canvas, or a shaped support, of 1.5m or more on one side.

principles.rule: Repeat one stripe or unit 8–40 times at an exact step, with a tolerance of 1mm.
Make the pattern symmetric about the centre axis, or repeat it with a shift of one step.
Hold 1 unit width and 1–2 hues across the picture, and allow a change of only one variable at a time.
Leave 0–20% as bare ground, with an even strip of 5–20mm between the units.
Keep a value gap of 20% or less between neighbouring units, or 80% or more for a black and white pair.
Set the unit width to a simple ratio, such as 1:2 or 1:3, of the gap and of the canvas.

palette.strategy: One to three flat hues or neutrals, used as they come, in strict order; grey, black and white are as strong as colour.
palette.distribution: 1–2 main hues 80–95%, a ground or a gap 5–20%, no accent.
palette.ground: Primed white or raw canvas, left bare in the gap.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Enamel, house paint, acrylic and thin oil; graphite for a fine grid.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Primed canvas, a shaped stretcher or a flat panel, 1.5m or more wide.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: None in view: flat, even coats with a roller or a brush, and masked edges.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: 2–3 even coats; no texture, no glaze, no correction in view.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Sharp, masked, with a tolerance of 1mm; the edge of the stripe is the line.

light_and_modelling.light: Even and neutral; the picture is lit like a wall.
light_and_modelling.modelling: None; each unit is a flat colour.
light_and_modelling.shadow: None; the shaped support may cast a real shadow on the wall.
light_and_modelling.temperature: Neutral; a single warm or cool hue in the whole picture.

subject.typical: Concentric stripes, parallel bands, a grid of fine pencil lines, a notched shape, a single bar.
subject.figure_scale: No figure; the unit is a stripe of 40–80mm repeated across the picture.
subject.treatment: Plain, exact and cool; the picture is an object, and the title is a number or a place.

surface.texture: Smooth and flat; a faint grain of the canvas in view; graphite lines of 0.2mm.

works.work: De la nada vida a la nada muerte

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API. None of the three works is flagged as public domain by the museum: the ids identify them only. Look at the museum page for the image and its licence; do not copy it.

emotion.target_response: Stillness and clarity: the viewer sees the thing as it is, and feels order without a message.

use_cases: interface and brand systems built on grids
packaging with one hue and one rule
avoid_when: The brief needs warmth, story, a figure or a hand-made touch.
The picture must show rich colour or texture.

modifiers.how: Soften the edge to 20–60mm, enlarge the field to 2m or more, saturate the hue, and stain the paint into raw cloth.
Drop the repeat; use 1–5 tilted shapes at 10–45° on a white field, and keep 50–70% of the picture empty.

brush_size.note: Rollers and masked edges leave no stroke in view.
